st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the paprika and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the beef, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 cup]] broth and simmer 30 minutes until the beef is tender and the liquid is reduced.
Sprinkle the gelatin over the hot stew and stir until dissolved. Fold in the potatoes, peas and raisins.
Spread the filling in a pan and chill at least 2 hours until firm, which keeps the juices inside.
For the dough, rub [[0.5 cup]] cold butter into [[4 cups]] flour, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt until crumbly.
Mix in the yolks and about [[0.75 cup]] warm water to make a smooth, firm dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough thin and cut 12 circles about 6 inches wide.
Put a spoonful of cold filling and a few chopped eggs on each circle. Fold over and pinch the edge into a tight braided seam.
Set the pastries on a lined tray, brush with beaten egg, and bake 20 to 25 minutes until deep gold.
Cool 10 minutes before eating, because the filling is very hot and juicy.

ing: aji amarillo or hot chili peppers
st: Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a heavy pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the potatoes 8 to 10 minutes until golden, then drain and salt with [[0.5 tsp]] of salt.
Season the beef with [[1 tsp]] salt, pepper and cumin.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over high heat and brown the beef 4 to 5 minutes. Remove it.
In the same pan, cook the sausage slices 3 minutes until browned.
Add the onion, tomatoes, garlic and chilies and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Return the beef, add [[0.5 tsp]] salt and optional [[1 tbsp]] mustard, and toss 2 minutes until hot.
Pile the fries on a platter and top with the beef mixture.
Add the halved eggs on top and serve right away.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Cook the rice with [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt, covered, over low heat for 15 minutes.
Pound each beef slice between plastic wrap to about 1/8 inch thick and sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Beat [[4 eggs]] in a shallow dish. Dredge the beef in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry each cutlet 2 minutes per side until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Toss the tomato, onion, parsley, [[1 tbsp]] vinegar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt for the salad.
Fry the potato slices in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 4 minutes until browned, then fry the other [[4 eggs]] in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Plate rice and potatoes, lay a cutlet over them, top with a fried egg and the salad.

ing: 2 diced for soup, rest cut into fries
st: Simmer the ribs in [[8 cups]] water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 1 hour until tender, skimming foam.
Blend the peanuts with [[1 cup]] of the broth until smooth.
In a large pot, cook the onion and garlic in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin.
Add the peanut puree, the remaining broth and ribs, carrots, and diced potatoes. Simmer 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and peas and simmer 8 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Meanwhile, fry the potato sticks in [[1 cup]] oil at 350°F (175°C) for 7 minutes until crisp. Drain and salt lightly.
Season the soup with [[1 tsp]] salt and stir in the parsley.
Ladle into bowls and top with fries.

ing: finely shredded; or use leftover roast beef
st: Soak the jerky in hot water for 20 minutes, drain, and shred finely. Squeeze dry.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a pot and fry the shredded jerky 5 minutes until lightly crisp. Set aside half.
Add the onion, tomatoes, garlic and cumin to the pot and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in [[2 cups]] rice for 1 minute, then add [[4 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low for 18 minutes until the rice is tender. Rest 5 minutes.
Fry the plantain slices in [[3 tbsp]] oil for 3 minutes per side until deep gold.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set, seasoning with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Top the rice with the saved jerky, plantains and a fried egg.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 4 minutes per side. Remove it.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, aji paste, cumin and oregano and cook 3 minutes.
Add [[2 cups]] broth and the chicken. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer 20 minutes until tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Add the peas and cook 5 minutes. Season with [[1 tsp]] salt.
Serve over [[3 cups]] cooked rice.

ing: trimmed of fat and silver skin, cut in 1-inch cubes; or use sirloin
st: Whisk the vinegar, garlic, cumin, chili paste, oil, oregano, salt and pepper into a marinade.
Add the beef heart, toss to coat, and marinate in the fridge for 4 hours or overnight.
Boil the potatoes in salted water 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Thread the meat onto skewers.
Heat a grill or grill pan to high.
Grill the skewers 3 to 4 minutes per side, brushing with extra marinade for the first half only, until charred and cooked through.
Rest the skewers for 3 minutes so the juices settle.
Serve the skewers with the boiled potatoes and llajua if desired.

ing: seeds removed; use red jalapenos or Fresno chilies
st: Wear gloves and remove the seeds from the chilies for a milder salsa.
Chop the chilies and tomatoes roughly.
Pound the chilies and tomatoes in a mortar, or pulse in a blender 5 to 6 times, until a chunky red puree forms.
Stir in the quilquina, onion and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Add the optional lime juice and taste.
Serve right away, or chill 20 minutes to blend the flavor.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Combine [[2 cups]] cassava starch, both cheeses, baking powder and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Beat the eggs with [[4 tbsp]] melted butter and [[0.33 cup]] warm milk.
Pour into the dry mix and knead by hand 3 minutes into a soft, slightly crumbly dough. Add a splash more milk if it will not hold together.
Roll into 20 balls or small rings about 2 inches wide.
Place on the sheet 2 inches apart.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and lightly golden.
Cool 5 minutes and serve warm, since they turn hard when cold.
Simmer [[4 cups]] of the water with the cinnamon and cloves in a pot for 10 minutes.
Whisk [[1 cup]] purple corn flour into [[2 cups]] cold water until no lumps remain.
Remove the spices, then slowly pour the corn mixture into the pot, whisking constantly.
Add [[0.5 cup]] sugar and a pinch of salt.
Cook on medium-low 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick like a thin custard.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice.
Serve hot in mugs, traditionally with a pastry such as buñuelos.
